description: CI/CD & DevSecOps: Setup Docker (multi-stage Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml for dev, docker-compose.prod.yml for production), GitHub Actions workflows (ci.yml for lint/test/security on PRs, cd.yml for Docker build and deployment on push to main, dependency-review.yml for vulnerability scanning), code quality configs (ESLint, Prettier, Jest), comprehensive documentation (README.md with setup/deployment instructions, SECURITY.md with security policy, CODEOWNERS, pull_request_template.md), and final verification (full test suite, security audit, staging deployment). This completes the DevSecOps infrastructure and project documentation.
steps: 1. Create Dockerfile at root with multi-stage build: Stage 1 'build-client' (Node base image, WORKDIR /app, COPY client/package*.json, RUN npm ci, COPY client/, RUN npm run build, output to /app/client/build). Stage 2 'production' (Node slim image, WORKDIR /app, COPY server/package*.json, RUN npm ci --only=production, COPY server/, COPY --from=build-client /app/client/build ./client/build, EXPOSE 5000, CMD ['node', 'server.js']). Create .dockerignore at root (node_modules, .git, .env, .env.*, coverage, build, dist, *.log, README.md, .github, .vscode).

2. Create docker-compose.yml at root for local dev: services 'app' (build from Dockerfile, ports 3000:3000 and 5000:5000, environment from .env files or env_file directive, depends_on mongo, volumes for bind mount source code hot reload) and 'mongo' (image: mongo:latest, ports 27017:27017, volumes for data persistence ./mongo-data:/data/db). Networks: app and mongo on default bridge network. MONGODB_URI in app env: mongodb://mongo:27017/portfolio_db.

3. Create docker-compose.prod.yml at root for production: services 'app' (same build, no bind mounts, restart: always, resource limits: memory 512M, cpus 0.5, environment from .env.production file) and 'mongo' (same, persistent volume, restart: always, resource limits). Create .env.production.example template with production env vars (MongoDB Atlas URI, Cloudinary, email SMTP, frontend URL, JWT secret).

4. Create .github/workflows/ci.yml: triggers on pull_request to main. Jobs: 1. 'lint' (checkout code, setup Node 18, npm ci in root, run npm run lint:client and npm run lint:server - add these scripts to root package.json running eslint in each workspace, run prettier --check .), 2. 'test-client' (checkout, setup Node, npm ci, run npm run test:client, upload coverage artifact), 3. 'test-server' (checkout, setup Node, npm ci, run npm run test:server with coverage, fail if coverage <70%, upload coverage artifact), 4. 'security' (checkout, setup Node, npm ci, run npm audit --audit-level=high in both workspaces, run Snyk test using snyk/actions/node@master with SNYK_TOKEN secret), 5. 'build' (checkout, setup Node, npm ci, run npm run build:all to verify build passes). Use matrix strategy for Node versions 18 and 20. All jobs must pass for PR to be mergeable.

5. Create .github/workflows/cd.yml: triggers on push to main. Jobs: 1. 'build-and-push' (checkout, setup Docker Buildx, login to Docker registry using secrets DOCKER_USERNAME and DOCKER_PASSWORD, build Docker image with tags commit SHA and 'latest', push to registry), 2. 'deploy' (depends_on build-and-push, checkout, deploy step using deployment target - Railway/Render webhook trigger with API key secret, or SSH to VPS with DEPLOY_SSH_KEY secret to pull image and restart containers, or AWS ECS task definition update). Document deployment setup in README.

6. Create .github/workflows/dependency-review.yml: triggers on pull_request. Uses actions/dependency-review-action@v3 to scan dependency changes in PR, fails if high or critical vulnerabilities introduced.

7. Create .eslintrc.js at root (or separate in client/ and server/): client extends ['react-app', 'react-app/jest'], server extends ['eslint:recommended'], add rules for code quality (no-unused-vars: error, no-console: warn for production, etc.). Create .prettierrc at root: {"semi": true, "singleQuote": true, "printWidth": 100, "tabWidth": 2}. Create .editorconfig at root: root=true, [*] indent_style=space, indent_size=2, charset=utf-8, trim_trailing_whitespace=true, insert_final_newline=true. Update server/jest.config.js with coverage thresholds: branches 70, functions 70, lines 70, statements 70. Add lint scripts to root package.json.

8. Create comprehensive README.md at root replacing CRA boilerplate: Sections: Project overview (brief description, screenshot/demo link, features list), Tech stack table (Frontend: React 18/Tailwind, Backend: Node.js/Express/MongoDB, Auth: JWT/bcrypt, Upload: Cloudinary/Multer, Email: Nodemailer, DevOps: Docker/GitHub Actions), Architecture diagram (embed Mermaid from implementation_plan or create new), Prerequisites (Node.js ≥18, MongoDB Atlas account or local MongoDB, Cloudinary account, SMTP email provider), Installation instructions (clone repo, npm run install:all, copy .env.example to .env in client/ and server/ and fill values, run seed scripts node server/scripts/createAdmin.js, npm run start:all), Development section (dev server commands, test commands, lint commands), Deployment section (Docker instructions: docker-compose up, Railway/Render setup steps with screenshots, environment variables list), API Documentation (link to endpoints list or embed brief reference), Contributing (link to CONTRIBUTING.md if exists or inline guidelines), License (MIT or chosen license). Available in French and English.

9. Create SECURITY.md at root: Sections: Supported Versions (table showing which versions receive security updates), Reporting a Vulnerability (instructions to report via private email or GitHub Security Advisories, response time expectations), Security Features (list: Helmet.js for HTTP headers, CORS origin restrictions, rate limiting 100 req/15min, JWT authentication 24h expiration, bcrypt password hashing 12 rounds, Joi input validation, mongo-sanitize NoSQL injection prevention, HPP parameter pollution prevention, Cloudinary secure file upload, HTTPS required in production), Security Best Practices for Deployment (env vars never in code, use strong JWT_SECRET minimum 32 chars, MongoDB Atlas IP whitelist, HTTPS via reverse proxy Nginx or platform SSL, regular npm audit and Snyk scans, update dependencies regularly, backup MongoDB data). Contact email for security concerns.

10. Create .github/CODEOWNERS: assign code ownership (e.g., '* @cabrelngamaleu' for all files, or specific paths like 'server/ @cabrelngamaleu' and 'client/ @cabrelngamaleu'). Create .github/pull_request_template.md: PR template with sections: Description (what changed), Type of Change (checkboxes: bugfix, feature, breaking change, documentation), Testing (how was this tested, test coverage for new code), Checklist (checkboxes: tests pass locally, lint passes, no console errors, screenshots for UI changes, documentation updated, self-review completed).

11. Create server/scripts/seedProjects.js (optional) to insert sample projects using existing workImg* images from client/src/assets/work/. Create server/scripts/seedBlog.js (optional) to insert sample blog posts. Update README with instructions to run optional seed scripts for demo data. Ensure scripts are idempotent (check if data exists before inserting, or add 'seed' field to identify seed data for easy cleanup).

12. Run full test suite: npm run test:all from root, verify client tests pass (if any), verify server tests pass with coverage ≥70% (npm test -- --coverage in server/, open coverage/lcov-report/index.html to review). If coverage below 70%, add tests to critical untested code paths (controllers, middleware, models). Fix any failing tests. Verify CI workflow locally if possible (using act or similar tool).

13. Perform security audit: run npm audit in client/ and server/, fix or acknowledge high/critical vulnerabilities, run Snyk scan (snyk test if Snyk CLI installed), manual security checklist (verify .env excluded from git: git log --all --full-history -- '**/.env' should be empty, verify JWT_SECRET is strong ≥32 chars in .env, verify CORS FRONTEND_URL configured correctly, test Helmet headers present: curl -I http://localhost:5000/api/projects and check X-Content-Type-Options/X-Frame-Options/etc., verify rate limiting: send 101 rapid requests and confirm 429, verify input validation: send malformed data to API and confirm 400 errors, verify file upload restrictions: try uploading non-image file to /api/projects and confirm rejection, verify mongo-sanitize: try NoSQL injection in message field '{ "$gt": "" }' and confirm sanitized). Document findings in .agents/tasks/security-audit.md.

14. Deploy to staging environment (Railway or Render): create account, create new project/service, connect GitHub repo (auto-deploy on push to main), configure environment variables (copy from .env.example, use MongoDB Atlas connection string, Cloudinary credentials, email SMTP settings, set NODE_ENV=production), configure build command (npm run install:all && npm run build:all) and start command (node server/server.js), deploy and verify deployment succeeds. Access staging URL, perform smoke tests: load homepage (all sections render), test contact form submission (verify email received), login to dashboard, create project with image upload (verify Cloudinary upload), create blog post with Markdown, submit message and verify appears in inbox, check Analytics page. Run Lighthouse audit on staging URL (aim for >80 Performance, >90 Accessibility, >90 Best Practices, >90 SEO). Document staging URL and deployment steps in .agents/tasks/deployment.md.

15. Final integration testing: execute end-to-end test scenarios from plan.md step 46 (public portfolio navigation, contact form, admin login, dashboard CRUD operations, responsive testing 320px/768px/1920px, security testing protected routes and rate limiting). Document any bugs found in .agents/tasks/testing-results.md, fix bugs, re-test. Verify all items in Post-Implementation Checklist from plan.md are complete.
acceptance_criteria: Dockerfile builds successfully: docker build -t cabrel-portfolio . completes without errors, image size reasonable (<500MB), docker run container serves app correctly on :5000

docker-compose.yml works for dev: docker-compose up --build starts both app and mongo containers, app connects to MongoDB, hot reload works (edit file, container detects change), data persists after container restart (stop and restart, verify MongoDB data not lost)

docker-compose.prod.yml works for production: docker-compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d starts containers in detached mode, containers remain running (docker ps), restart policy works (manually stop container, verify it restarts automatically), resource limits applied (docker stats shows memory/CPU limits)

CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) passes: create test PR, verify workflow triggers on GitHub Actions tab, verify all jobs pass (lint, test-client, test-server with coverage ≥70%, security npm audit + Snyk, build), verify PR blocked if any job fails (test by creating PR with lint error), coverage reports uploaded as artifacts

CD workflow (.github/workflows/cd.yml) succeeds: merge PR to main, verify workflow triggers, verify Docker image built and pushed to registry (check Docker Hub/GHCR for image with commit SHA tag and 'latest' tag), verify deployment succeeds (check deployment platform logs or SSH to server, verify app running with new image), access deployed app URL and verify functionality
dependency-review workflow works: create PR adding dependency with known vulnerability, verify workflow runs and flags vulnerability in Actions summary
ESLint configured: npm run lint:client and npm run lint:server commands work (add to root package.json), fix all lint errors in codebase, verify CI uses these commands
Prettier configured: npm run format (or prettier --check .) command works, all code formatted consistently, verify CI checks formatting
Jest coverage thresholds enforced: run npm test -- --coverage in server/, verify coverage ≥70% for branches/functions/lines/statements, verify test fails if coverage below threshold

README.md complete: includes all required sections (overview, tech stack, architecture, prerequisites, installation, development, deployment, API docs, contributing, license), instructions clear and accurate (test by following from scratch or have someone else follow), both French and English versions (or French primary with English key sections)

SECURITY.md complete: includes supported versions, vulnerability reporting instructions, security features list (all 10+ features from implementation actually implemented), deployment best practices, security contact
CODEOWNERS and PR template created: test PR auto-requests review from CODEOWNERS, PR template auto-populates on new PR with checklist

Seed scripts created and documented: server/scripts/createAdmin.js creates default admin (test on empty DB, verify admin created and can login), optional seedProjects.js and seedBlog.js insert sample data, README includes seed script instructions
Full test suite passes: npm run test:all succeeds, server tests show ≥70% coverage, all tests green, no failing tests

Security audit complete: npm audit clean or vulnerabilities acknowledged/patched, Snyk scan clean or issues triaged, manual security checklist all items verified (no .env in git, JWT secret strong, CORS configured, Helmet headers present, rate limiting works, input validation works, file upload restricted, NoSQL injection prevented), findings documented

Staging deployment successful: app deployed to Railway or Render, accessible via staging URL, smoke tests pass (load pages, submit forms, login, CRUD operations all work), Lighthouse audit scores >80 Performance, >90 Accessibility/Best Practices/SEO, deployment steps documented

End-to-end testing complete: all test scenarios from plan.md step 46 executed and pass, responsive testing at all breakpoints verified, security testing (protected routes, rate limiting) verified, bugs documented and fixed, testing results documented in .agents/tasks/testing-results.md
verification: Run docker build -t cabrel-portfolio . from root, verify build completes without errors, check final image size with docker images | grep cabrel-portfolio (should be <500MB ideally), run docker run -p 5000:5000 --env-file server/.env cabrel-portfolio, access http://localhost:5000 in browser, verify frontend loads and backend APIs respond

Run docker-compose up --build from root, check console logs for both app and mongo containers starting, verify 'MongoDB connected' log, access http://localhost:3000 (client) and http://localhost:5000 (server), test API calls work, edit a client file (e.g., change text in HeroSection.jsx), save, verify container detects change and reloads (check logs), stop containers (Ctrl+C), run docker-compose up again, verify MongoDB data persists (projects/blog/messages still there)

Run docker-compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --build, run docker ps and verify both app and mongo containers running, run docker stop <app-container-id>, wait 10 seconds, run docker ps again and verify container restarted automatically (restart policy), run docker stats and verify resource limits applied (memory ~512M, CPU <1.0)

Push branch and create PR on GitHub, go to Actions tab, verify ci workflow triggered, wait for all jobs to complete, verify all pass (green checkmarks), check coverage artifacts uploaded (click workflow run, see artifacts section), intentionally create PR with ESLint error (e.g., add console.log without use), verify lint job fails and PR shows failure status

Merge PR to main branch, go to Actions tab, verify cd workflow triggered, wait for build-and-push job to complete, check Docker registry (Docker Hub, GHCR, or AWS ECR) for new image with commit SHA tag and 'latest' tag, wait for deploy job to complete, check deployment platform (Railway/Render dashboard or SSH to VPS), verify app restarted with new image, access production/staging URL and verify app works

Create test PR adding a package with known vulnerability (e.g., old version of express), go to Actions tab, verify dependency-review workflow runs, check workflow summary for vulnerability warning/failure

Run npm run lint:client from root, verify ESLint runs on client code, run npm run lint:server, verify ESLint runs on server code, fix any errors reported, verify CI workflow uses these commands in lint job
Run npx prettier --check . from root, verify Prettier checks all files, fix any formatting issues with npx prettier --write ., commit formatted code, verify CI workflow checks formatting

Run cd server && npm test -- --coverage, verify coverage report shows ≥70% for all metrics (branches, functions, lines, statements), open coverage/lcov-report/index.html in browser to review detailed coverage, if any metric below 70% verify tests fail with error

Open README.md in GitHub (or render locally with Markdown viewer), verify all sections present and complete, follow installation instructions from scratch on fresh clone (or ask team member to test), verify commands work and app starts successfully, check for any broken links or incorrect commands

Open SECURITY.md in GitHub, verify all required sections present, verify security features list matches actually implemented features (cross-check with code: Helmet in server.js, CORS configured, rate-limiter applied, JWT auth in auth middleware, bcrypt in User model, Joi in validate middleware, mongo-sanitize in security middleware, HPP in security middleware, Cloudinary in upload, HTTPS in deployment), verify contact email provided
Create test PR, verify CODEOWNERS triggers review request (check PR sidebar for requested reviewers), verify PR description auto-populates with template checklist (checkboxes for tests, lint, etc.)

Delete User collection in MongoDB, run node server/scripts/createAdmin.js, verify console log confirms admin created, use Postman to POST /api/auth/login with default credentials (check script for username/password), verify successful login with token, optionally run node server/scripts/seedProjects.js and seedBlog.js, verify sample data appears in database and app

Run npm run test:all from root, verify both client and server tests execute, verify all tests pass (green output, 0 failures), check server coverage ≥70% (npm test -- --coverage in server/), if any failures fix tests and re-run

Run npm audit in client/ and server/, review vulnerabilities, fix high/critical or document why acceptable, run snyk test in both (if Snyk CLI installed), review findings, execute manual checklist: run git log --all --full-history -- '**/.env' and verify no results (no .env in history), check .env files for JWT_SECRET length ≥32 chars, verify CORS FRONTEND_URL in server/.env matches client URL, curl -I http://localhost:5000/api/projects and verify X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and X-Frame-Options in response headers, use Postman runner or bash loop to send 101 requests to any endpoint and verify 101st returns 429, send POST /api/projects with invalid data (missing required field) and verify 400 with validation error, try uploading .txt file as project image and verify rejection, send POST /api/messages with body {"message": {"$gt": ""}} and verify sanitized (no error, message stored as string), document all findings in .agents/tasks/security-audit.md

Go to Railway.app or Render.com, create account, create new project, connect GitHub repo, configure environment variables (MongoDB Atlas URI, Cloudinary, email, frontend URL, JWT secret, NODE_ENV=production), set build command 'npm run install:all && npm run build:all' and start command 'node server/server.js', trigger deploy, wait for deployment to complete (check platform logs), access staging URL, test: load homepage (all sections render without errors), fill contact form and submit (verify email received in inbox), navigate to /login, login with admin credentials, navigate to /dashboard/projects, click add project, upload image file, fill form, submit (verify project created and image shows Cloudinary URL), navigate to /dashboard/blog, create post with Markdown (test **bold** and # heading), verify live preview works, publish post, go back to public portfolio and verify post appears, open DevTools and run Lighthouse audit (click lighthouse tab, select all categories, generate report), verify scores >80 Performance, >90 Accessibility, >90 Best Practices, >90 SEO, document staging URL and deployment steps in .agents/tasks/deployment.md

Execute all test scenarios from plan.md step 46: 1. Public portfolio - navigate through all sections, click project cards, read blog, submit contact. 2. Login - access /dashboard without auth (verify redirect), login (verify redirect to dashboard). 3. Overview - verify stats display. 4. Projects - create/edit/delete/reorder projects with image upload. 5. Blog - create/edit/delete posts with Markdown. 6. Messages - verify contact submissions appear, mark read, delete. 7. Analytics - verify graphs display data. 8. Profile - change password, logout, login with new password. 9. Responsive - test at 320px (iPhone SE), 768px (iPad), 1920px (desktop) using DevTools responsive mode, verify all pages usable. 10. Security - test protected routes without auth (expect 401/redirect), test rate limiting (send 101 requests, expect 429). Document any bugs in .agents/tasks/testing-results.md, fix bugs, re-test until all scenarios pass
